definitions: To have a very difficult act to follow, usually because a predecessor was exceptionally successful.
To be in a position where one is expected to meet very high standards set by someone who came before them.
examples: The new CEO will have huge boots to fill after the founder's incredible run.
Taking over as captain, she knew she had huge boots to fill.
He has huge boots to fill, replacing a legend like that.
synonyms: have a tough act to follow
